title: Work and jobs (Beruf und Arbeit)
summary: Say what you do, where you work and what you study, and ask others the same.
goals: Say your job and where you work
Use arbeiten and machen in every person
Use male and female job names (-in)

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 9: Working life (Ich bin Lehrerin, Mein Beruf)

points: Every job has a masculine form with [[der]] and a feminine form with [[die]]. Mostly the feminine adds -in: [[der Lehrer]], [[die Lehrerin]].
Some get an umlaut as well: [[der Arzt]], [[die Ärztin]] (doctor); [[der Koch]], [[die Köchin]] (cook).
Jobs from English keep their English sound and still add -in: [[der Manager]], [[die Managerin]].

The video's list: [[Pilot]], [[Architekt]], [[Programmierer]], [[Fotograf]], [[Polizist]], [[Journalist]], [[Sänger]] (singer), [[Tänzer]] (dancer), [[Buchhalter]] (accountant), [[Dolmetscher]] (interpreter), all with -in for women.
To ask: [[Was sind Sie von Beruf?]] The answer has no article: [[Ich bin Lehrer.]]

phrases.en: What do you do for a living? (polite)

points: [[das Studienfach]], plural [[die Studienfächer]]: a subject at university.
Humanities ([[die Geisteswissenschaften]]): [[Kunst]], [[Theater]], [[Geschichte]] (history, and also 'story'), [[Philosophie]], [[Musikwissenschaft]], modern languages.

What you study: [[Was studierst du?]] (polite [[Was studieren Sie?]]) - [[Ich studiere Architektur.]] For later: [[Was willst du studieren?]] - [[Ich will Medizin studieren.]] or [[Ich möchte Medizin studieren.]]
Where: [[Wo studierst du?]] - [[an der Universität Berlin]]. [[die Universität]] and [[die Hochschule]] mean the same; a university of applied sciences is [[die Fachhochschule]].
All in one sentence: [[Ich studiere Informatik an der Universität Bonn.]]

phrases.de: Ich studiere an der Fachhochschule Berlin.
phrases.en: I study at the University of Applied Sciences Berlin.

phrases.de: Ich studiere Informatik an der Universität Bonn.
phrases.en: I study computer science at the University of Bonn.

notes.extra: Words for university subjects, and [[an der Universität]] for where you study.

points: Every noun has an article, but in some places German leaves it out. Jobs are only one case.
Names, nationalities and jobs: [[Guten Morgen, Frau Schmidt.]], [[Sie ist Japanerin.]], [[Ich bin Architektin.]]
Plurals in general, and things you can't count: [[Ich liebe Tiere.]], [[Hast du Geld?]], [[Er hat Angst.]] (he's afraid)
Materials: [[Die Kette ist aus Gold.]], [[Der Pullover ist aus Wolle.]]
Illnesses: [[Eva hat Fieber.]] (Eva has a temperature)
After an amount: [[ein Kilo Äpfel]]. And headlines and adverts often drop articles too.
Most countries and all cities: [[Ich komme aus Deutschland.]], [[Sabine fährt nach München.]] A few countries keep theirs: [[die Schweiz]], [[die Türkei]].

The necklace is made of gold.

phrases.de: Ich hätte gern ein Kilo Äpfel.
phrases.en: I'd like a kilo of apples.

notes.extra: The other cases without an article: plurals, money and feelings, materials, illnesses, amounts, cities.

sections.title: Talking about work
sections.text:
- [[Was sind Sie von Beruf?]] or [[Was machst du beruflich?]] - What do you do?
- [[Ich bin Entwickler.]] - I'm a developer.
- [[Ich arbeite als Entwickler.]] - I work as a developer.
- [[Ich arbeite bei Siemens.]] - I work at Siemens.
- [[Ich studiere Informatik.]] - I study computer science.

[[bei]] + company, [[in]] + city: [[Ich arbeite bei Siemens in München.]]

sections.title: No 'a' before jobs
sections.text: German says [[Ich bin Entwickler.]] with no article, where English says 'I am **a** developer'. Russian works the same way (Я программист), so this one is easy for you.

sections.title: Male and female job names
sections.text:
Most job names have a female form with **-in**:

- [[der Entwickler]] - [[die Entwicklerin]]
- [[der Lehrer]] - [[die Lehrerin]]
- [[der Student]] - [[die Studentin]]

The plural of the -in forms ends in **-innen**: [[die Lehrerinnen]]. In job ads you will also see forms like 'Entwickler (m/w/d)', which means the job is open to everyone.
Verbs whose stem ends in **t** or **d** add an extra **e** so you can pronounce them: [[du arbeitest]], [[er arbeitet]] (not 'arbeitst', 'arbeitt'). Same for [[antworten]]: [[du antwortest]].

sections.title: In tech
sections.text: In Munich tech companies, English job titles are normal German: 'Ich arbeite als Data Scientist' or 'Ich bin Software Engineer' are perfectly fine sentences.
